records.Concise description: One of the earliest public Lightning Network search and analysis services for nodes, channels, capacity, and graph-derived statistics.
records.Deeper researched summary: 1ML provides a public interface for searching Lightning nodes and channels and displays aggregate public-graph statistics. It remains reachable and serving current-looking network data in 2026, preserving historical continuity as an early Lightning explorer. However, current operator/development documentation is comparatively sparse, so MSC treats its lifecycle as active service operation while keeping source confidence MEDIUM. Its published node, channel, and capacity figures are public-graph observations and must not be treated as complete Lightning-network totals.
Creators / founders: Current operator identity not clearly documented in first-party material reviewed
records.Launch / history: 1ML became a prominent Lightning search/analysis engine during the network's early public growth and remains publicly accessible in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It provides historical continuity for how operators and users have observed public Lightning topology and complements newer analytics platforms such as Amboss.

Official sources.label: 1ML public Lightning search and analysis service

records.Verification basis: The live first-party service was verified in August 2026; current operator/development provenance remains less transparent than HIGH-confidence open-source projects.
Research notes / uncertainties: MEDIUM confidence reflects sparse first-party operator/development documentation, not an uncertain service lifecycle.
Published public capacity excludes private channels and does not equal total Lightning liquidity.
Do not freeze current node/channel/capacity numbers into timeless copy.

records.Concise description: A long-running Bitcoin dashboard that aggregates chain, network, market, mining, and monetary metrics into a single-page observational interface.
records.Deeper researched summary: Clark Moody Bitcoin traces its history to an early 2011 real-time Bitcoin market-data site and now offers a broad dashboard spanning Bitcoin network and ecosystem metrics. It is valuable as an observational system and historical data-interface lineage, but its individual fields pull from multiple underlying data sources and should not be mistaken for native Bitcoin protocol state. The site is operational in 2026, while public project/release documentation is sparse enough to retain MEDIUM confidence for current implementation details.
records.Launch / history: Clark Moody launched Bitcoin market-data tooling in 2011. The current Bitcoin dashboard evolved into a broad single-page ecosystem metrics interface and remains available in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the longest-running independent Bitcoin data interfaces and illustrates how network, chain, market, and mining data can be assembled into an operational overview.
records.Verification basis: Current hosted site and first-party history page establish continued service operation and the project's 2011 lineage; implementation/source details are less comprehensively documented.
Research notes / uncertainties: Dashboard fields may combine protocol data, estimates, exchange data, or third-party feeds; do not label the whole dashboard as consensus state.
MEDIUM confidence reflects sparse current implementation documentation, not an uncertain service lifecycle.

records.Concise description: A Rust Electrum server implementation that indexes Bitcoin Core data for efficient wallet and address-history queries.
records.Deeper researched summary: electrs connects to a local Bitcoin full node and builds an index optimized for serving Electrum protocol queries, including script/address history and mempool-related lookups. It is widely used in self-hosted node stacks and as a backend component for explorers. The project explicitly optimizes for personal or smaller-scale deployments rather than claiming to be the only Electrum server architecture. Release 0.11.1 in February 2026 confirms current maintenance.
records.Launch / history: electrs emerged as a Rust alternative Electrum server and became widely integrated into personal-node distributions. Version 0.11.1 was released February 22, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a major bridge between full-node data and lightweight wallet queries and is a common backend for private/self-hosted wallet infrastructure.
records.Verification basis: Official repository and February 2026 release notes establish active maintenance, architecture, and indexer role.
Research notes / uncertainties: electrs-derived address/history results are indexer state built from node data, not an additional consensus layer.
Do not imply every Esplora deployment uses this exact electrs configuration.

records.Concise description: A mature Python Electrum server that indexes full-node blockchain data to answer arbitrary wallet history queries efficiently.
records.Deeper researched summary: ElectrumX connects to a full node, indexes blockchain data, and serves the Electrum protocol to public or private wallet clients. The current repository is maintained under the Electrum/Spesmilo organization after the original upstream history diverged, making it an important server lineage distinct from the Electrum wallet itself. It is canonically NETWORK infrastructure; Electrum the client/wallet remains WALLETS.
records.Launch / history: ElectrumX was introduced in the mid-2010s as a scalable successor to earlier Electrum server software and remains actively maintained by the Electrum ecosystem.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It established a durable server architecture for wallet history queries and remains part of the infrastructure behind lightweight Bitcoin clients.
Important technical or cultural characte: Distinct from the Electrum wallet client
records.Verification basis: Current Spesmilo/Electrum-controlled repository establishes the maintained ElectrumX lineage and server role.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not duplicate Electrum wallet here; ElectrumX is the server/indexer profile.
Server-returned histories are derived indexes over node data, not separate consensus state.
